Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1. Heard Sri V.P. Srivastava, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Harish Chandra Mishra,
learned counsel for applicants and learned AGA appearing on behalf of State/opposite party no.1.
No one appeared on behalf of opposite party no.2 even in the revised call.

2. The present petition has been filed for seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceeding of Case No.3880 of 2009 (State Vs. Mukesh Chauhan and others), under Sections 120-B, 420, 427, 459, 471,
264, 265 IPC, Police Station Phugana, District Muzaffarnagar pending in the court of learned Special Chief Judicial Magistrate, Muzaffarnagar and chargesheet dated 09.04.2009 submitted in Case Crime No.39 of 2009, under Rules 31, 32, 33, 38A(2) clause 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 96(1)I.J. of Sugar Mukesh Chauhan And Another vs State Of U.P. 471, 264, 265 IPC, Police Station Phugana, District Muzaffarnagar.

3. Learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of applicants submitted that opposite party no.2 lodged an FIR on 16.02.2009 as Case Crime No.39 of 2009, under Rules 31, 32, 33, 38A(2) clause 1,
2, 3, 4, 5 and 96(1) I.J. of Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954 along with Sections 120-B, 420, 427, 459, 471, 264, 265 IPC, Police Station Phugana, District Muzaffarnagar.

sentences.text:
Learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of applicants submitted through the narration of FIR that opposite party no.2 along with one Mr. Veer Sen, Sugarcane Development Inspector made a sudden inspection of Purchase Center authorized to the applicants where the Cane Weighment Clerk Satish Kumar was found working and the standard of weigh bridge was checked by them and found weighing less amounting and the same was contrary to the Rules 31, 32, 33, 38A(2) clause 1, 2, 3, 4,
5 and 96(1) I.J. of Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954 and the same was also punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 427, 459, 471, 264, 265 IPC.
4.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: After recording statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the concerned Inquiry Officer preferred chargesheet dated 09.04.2009 in Case Crime No.39 of 2009, under Rules 31, 32, 33, 38A(2) clause 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 96(1) I.J. of Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954 along with Sections 120-B, 420, 427, 459, 471, 264, 265 IPC which impugned the present application.

entities.text: I.J. of Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
5. For seeking quashing of the said chargesheet along with entire criminal proceedings, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of applicants raised several other grounds inter-alia precisely the ground that applicant no.1 is occupier of Titawi Sugar Complex Titawi and applicant no.2 is whole time Director of Mawana Sugars Ltd. who appointed and deputed Sri Satish Kumar as a Weighment Clerk at the concerned Purchase Center for purchase and weighment of cane accurately,
strictly in accordance with the Rule 38-A of the U.P. Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954 (in short "Rules, 1954") but at the same time, learned Senior Counsel also submitted that the competent authority for appointment of Weighment Clerk is the Collector which is prescribed under Rule 120 of Rules, 1954 and no prosecution shall be instituted under this Rules unless the persons complained against has been given an opportunity by the Cane Commissioner or the District Magistrate to show cause why he should not be prosecuted.

entities.text: U.P. Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6 . Learned Senior Counsel submitted that as per Rules 33 and 33-A of Rules, 1954, there is a proper arrangement with regard to weighing the cane tendered by the vendor before the Purchase Center.

At the time of raising arguments with regard to challenging the entire proceedings carried out in shape of Case Crime No.39 of 2009, reliance has been placed over Rule 121 of Rules, 1954 wherein it has been specifically mentioned that no court shall take cognizance of any offence under the Act or these Rules except upon complaint made within one year of the date on which the offence is alleged to have been committed.

It is the contention of learned Senior Counsel that at no point of time, any show cause notice has ever been served upon the applicants in compliance with Rule 121 of Rules 1954 and lodging FIR is contrary to the provisions which is strictly applicable over the applicants.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA appearing on behalf of opposite party no.1 supported the stand taken up by learned counsel of opposite party no.2 through counter affidavit but at the same time, it has not Mukesh Chauhan And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163429684/
2 been disputed that the relevant provisions of Rules 1954 is strictly applicable in the present matter.

entities.text: Mukesh Chauhan And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. After hearing the rival submissions, it is crystal clear that there is hardly any provision available before the opposite party no.2 for institution of any criminal proceedings in shape of lodging the FIR, the provisions applicable in the instant matter is otherwise that without serving any show cause even no complaint can be instituted in respect of charges levelled against the applicants.
9.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and after considering the relevant provisions of Standard of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 along with the Rules, 1954 as discussed above, there is no occasion available before opposite party no.2 to pursue the proceedings initiated in shape of lodging FIR in Case Crime No.39 of 2009 and as such, entire criminal proceeding of Case No.3880 of 2009 (State Vs. Mukesh Chauhan and others), under Sections 120-B, 420, 427, 459, 471, 264, 265 IPC, Police Station Phugana, District Muzaffarnagar pending in the court of learned Special Chief Judicial Magistrate, Muzaffarnagar and chargesheet dated 09.04.2009 submitted in Case Crime No.39 of 2009, under Rules 31, 32, 33, 38A(2) clause 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 96(1)I.J. of Sugar Cane (Regulation of Purchase and Supply) Rules, 1954 and under Sections 120-B, 420, 427, 459, 471, 264,
265 IPC, Police Station Phugana, District Muzaffarnagar, are hereby quashed.
10.
